deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is building the basic vocabulary of stratified spaces for 'topologie modérée' (tame topology). On the previous page a space X carries an increasing filtration by closed subspaces X_i. The filtration is called equisingular if the diagram of closed subspaces (X_0 ⊂ X_1 ⊂ … ⊂ X) is equisingular along each difference V_i = X_i − X_{i−1}. 'Equisingular along' was defined on earlier pages, and presumably means local topological triviality of the whole diagram along the subspace. The connected components of the V_i are called 'feuilles' (strata). He has already shown that if the filtration is equisingular, the closure of a leaf is a union of leaves (the frontier condition).

On this page:
(1) Closed subsets that are unions of leaves are stable under arbitrary intersection and finite union. In particular, an intersection of closed leaves is a union of closed leaves.
(2) Inclusion of closures, F ≤ G iff F̄ ⊂ Ḡ, gives a partial order on leaves, called the 'relation d'incidence'. This is the modern poset of strata. The leaves incident to F and distinct from it have union F̄ − F, called the boundary bF. It is closed and a union of closed leaves.
(3) Proposition: a filtration is equisingular iff (a) the frontier condition holds and (b) the diagram made of X and all closed leaves F̄ (with the inclusion maps) is equisingular along every leaf. So equisingularity really belongs to the incidence diagram of strata, not to the chosen filtration.
(4) Definition: a partition (F_i) of X into 'leaves' is an equisingular partition if three conditions hold:
  1° each F_i is locally closed, i.e. F̄_i and bF_i = F̄_i − F_i are closed;
  2° the frontier condition holds;
  3° the diagram of X, the F̄_i and their inclusions is equisingular along each leaf.
  The margin adds that a partition satisfying 1° and 2° is called 'admissible'.

On the next page he explains why: different equisingular filtrations can give the same partition. In the 'par morceaux' (piecewise) context there are four canonical filtrations attached to one partition (by dimension, by successive minimal strata, and their duals). He then switches to the language of 'espaces à partitions équisingulières' and defines admissible systems of partitions on diagrams of spaces, i.e. stratified maps.

In modern terms: a stratified space as a poset-indexed decomposition into locally closed strata satisfying the frontier condition, plus a local-triviality (Thom–Mather / Siebenmann style) condition imposed on the whole diagram of closed strata.
errors: Gap: in the filtration setting, leaves are connected components of V_i. They are open in V_i, and hence locally closed with closed boundary, only if V_i is locally connected. The page asserts bF is closed without stating this hypothesis. The partition definition repairs it by imposing 1° explicitly.

The 'only if' direction of the proposition (equisingular filtration ⇒ the diagram of all closed leaves is equisingular) is stated without proof. It is plausible: locally the trivialization is a product, and closures of global leaves are locally unions of closures of local product pieces. But it depends on the precise definition of 'équisingulier le long de', which is not on this page.
Antisymmetry of the incidence order uses injectivity of F ↦ F̄, which was asserted on the previous page. That assertion is fine once leaves are locally closed and the frontier condition holds.

ideas.what: Leaves (strata) as connected components of successive differences of a closed filtration; closed leaves, boundary bF = F̄ − F; frontier condition derived from equisingularity
ideas.modern_name: Stratification with frontier condition; closed strata; link/boundary of a stratum
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and stratified structures informally; no formal definitions there

ideas.what: Incidence partial order on strata, F ≤ G iff F̄ ⊂ Ḡ
ideas.modern_name: Poset of strata / stratification over a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; systematized in poset-stratified spaces by Lurie (Higher Algebra App. A), Treumann, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Characterization: a filtration is equisingular iff frontier condition plus equisingularity (local triviality) of the full diagram of closed strata along each stratum; hence the partition, not the filtration, is the primary object
ideas.modern_name: Locally trivial / locally cone-like stratified space (Siebenmann CS-sets, Thom–Mather local triviality), filtration-independence of stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann (1972), Thom–Mather; filtration vs. poset viewpoint discussed by Goresky–MacPherson and later Lurie

ideas.what: Admissible partition (locally closed strata + frontier condition) as a weaker notion preceding equisingularity

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates equisingularity as a property of the whole diagram of closed strata (X with all F̄_i and inclusions), locally trivial along each stratum. The partition, not the filtration, is the intrinsic datum. This anticipates the 'stratification = poset-indexed decomposition' viewpoint later made standard (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It is not an unknown result, but it is an unpublished 1974 formulation of the foundations he later only sketched in the Esquisse.
missed.quote: le diagramme formé par X, les F̄_i et leurs inclusions est équisingulier le long de chaque feuille
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck's tame-topology program had concrete axiomatic foundations for stratified spaces (and, on the next page, stratified maps) by 1974. This is of historical interest for the o-minimal / tame geometry and stratified homotopy theory literature.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard stratification foundations (frontier condition, incidence poset, boundary of strata, filtration vs. partition), cleanly formulated. The diagram-equisingularity formulation is a nice historical detail, but specialists would recognize it as equivalent to known local-triviality notions.
transcription_corrections: Margin note likely reads 'si 1° et 2° sont satisfaits, on dira que la partition est admissible'. The '[V-]' prefix is probably a misreading, consistent with 'partition admissible' on the next page.
In condition 1° the boundary is written 'b F_i' (bF_i = F̄_i − F_i), consistent with the earlier definition of 'bord'.
The struck phrase in condition b) is hard to read ('localement plat le' / 'localement trivial le'?). It is replaced by 'équisingulier'.
'33' at the bottom is the folio number in the archive.
